title: Heading Error and Steering Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A compass dial, a step-by-step calculation panel, and two motor bars show how a heading-swarm follower computes the shortest-turn error with (target - current + 180) % 360 - 180 and turns it into clipped left and right motor speeds with steer(). A replay shows the robot turning, and oscillating when Kp is too high.

educational.topic: Wrap-around heading error and proportional steering
learningObjectives: Calculate the shortest-turn heading error with wrap-around using (target - current + 180) % 360 - 180.
Decide the turn direction from the sign of the error.
Predict the left and right motor values that steer() returns, including clipping to 0..1.
Identify a Kp value that makes the follower oscillate.
prerequisites: Arithmetic operators including % and functions with return values (Chapter 4)
PWM duty cycle and motor speed (Chapter 7)
standards: CSTA 3A-AP-13: Create prototypes that use algorithms to solve computational problems by leveraging prior student knowledge and personal interests.

controls.label: Play turn
controls.purpose: Replay the robot turning with the shown motor speeds until the error is under 2 degrees.

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Restore the default headings, base speed, and Kp.

controls.label: Compass arrows
controls.purpose: Drag the green (current) or purple (target) arrow to set a heading.

equations: error = (target - current + 180) mod 360 - 180 (floored modulo, as in Python)
left = clamp(base + turn, 0, 1); right = clamp(base - turn, 0, 1)
each 50 ms tick: heading += (left - right) * 20 degrees
assumptions: The robot turns in place at a rate proportional to the motor speed difference.
Heading measurements are exact (no sensor noise).
limitations: Wheel slip, motor dead band, and battery sag are not modeled.
The replay is shown at half speed so each tick is visible.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example with live, step-by-step intermediate values
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Direct manipulation (sliders and draggable arrows) with immediate calculation feedback and a replay
keyQuestions: Why is the error for current 350 and target 20 equal to +30 instead of -330?
Which motor is faster when the error is positive, and why?
At what Kp does the follower start swinging back and forth?
commonMisconceptions: The heading error is simply target - current (this sends the robot the long way around north).
Python's % works like JavaScript's % on negative numbers (Python's result is never negative for % 360).
A larger Kp always makes the robot line up faster (too large a Kp clips the motors and causes oscillation).
assessmentOpportunities: Hand-calculate three wrap-around errors and verify them in the panel.
Predict clipped motor values for a given error and Kp.
Find the smallest Kp that makes the replay oscillate.
